Berkshire Hathaway has climbed 14% in 2026 while the NASDAQ 100 tracker QQQ has gained just 1%, as an AI-driven tech sell-off erased most of its progress.

A conglomerate built over decades is beating the tech-heavy NASDAQ 100 in 2026, and the gap has widened as investors pull back from pricey growth stocks. Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRK-B) stock is up 14% year to date (YTD) to $571.46 in the latest session. That price includes a 0.1% dip from where shares last closed, and Berkshire has slipped over the past several sessions, so it hasn't been fully immune.

Mark Wilson / Getty Images

Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ), the fund that tracks the NASDAQ 100, is up 1% YTD to $622.41. The slim gain leaves the index looking stuck in place, since a steep tech sell-off this month has erased much of its 2026 progress. SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) sits in the middle, up 3% YTD to $701.80.

What Powered Berkshire Hathaway's Run in 2026

Berkshire's steady footing starts with its operating businesses. In a filing on August 11, the company said its Q2 2026 operating earnings, its preferred profit measure, rose to $12.98 billion from $11.16 billion a year earlier. BNSF, Berkshire Hathaway Energy and the manufacturing, service and retailing group all grew, while insurance underwriting and insurance investment income declined.

Key Takeaways

Constellation Energy fell 10% in the past week as AI stocks sold off, giving back most of its jump on a third-quarter beat and guidance raise.

NuScale, Oklo and Cameco fell even more, and most of the week's analyst news on Constellation was higher price targets.

Constellation's 15- and 20-year deals with Google and Amazon don't change with the market, but analysts' 2028 estimates still need new contracts.

With the stock below its usual forward multiple and estimates holding, it's a buy for patient investors ahead of 2027 guidance.

Constellation Energy (CEG:NASDAQ) is down 10% in the past week, and its own news doesn't explain it.

The stock fell with the AI trade, as the S&P 500 lost 5% and the Nasdaq 100 6% around Anthropic's IPO. Other nuclear names fell harder: NuScale Power (SMR:NYSE) lost 19%, Oklo (OKLO:NYSE) [12%] and uranium supplier Cameco (CCJ) 14%. That leaves Constellation near where it closed before its Nov. 9 report, giving back most of that day's 10% jump.

Wall Street mostly raised its targets

BMO Capital raised its target to $335 from $316 on Nov. 16, citing the above-market contracts added in the third quarter. Barclays went to $371 from $345 on Nov. 19. Bernstein moved the other way, trimming its target to $293 from $296 on Nov. 17, citing the election selloff. A $3 trim doesn't explain the drop.

Other nuclear names have more to prove

NuScale and Oklo are pitching reactors that aren't built yet, the exact risk investors were dumping. NuScale's third-quarter revenue fell to $0.3 million from $8.2 million a year earlier, and its partner ENTRA1 is still in talks with the Tennessee Valley Authority. Oklo held $3.1 billion of cash and securities at Sept. 30, and analysts expect it to burn about twice that from 2026 through 2030.

Cameco owns 49% of Westinghouse, whose growth rests on reactor orders not yet signed. Analysts expect Cameco's EPS to roughly double in 2027, and at 48x forward earnings, it needs that step to arrive on time.

The S&P 500 comes into today's session on a six-day losing streak.
Credit: Spencer Platt / Getty Images

Stock futures suggest the Nasdaq and S&P 500 will fall sharply in early trading; the major indexes are on track to have their worst week in about a year and one-half; Anthropic shares are falling in early trading after yesterday's massive IPO; Intuit's stock is plummeting after it announced plans to sell Mailchimp; and retailer stocks are moving at the end of a busy week of earnings reports from the sector.

Here's what you need to know today.

Stock Futures Point to Steep Declines

Two major stock indexes appear poised to extend yesterday's steep losses. Futures tied to the Nasdaq 100 were recently down 2.2% while those tied to the S&P 500 dropped 1.5%. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 0.5%. The S&P 500 enters today's session on a six-day losing streak, and all three major indexes are at their lowest levels since the spring. Meanwhile, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, which affects interest rates, fell to 4.98% from 5.05% Thursday. Oil prices were slipping, with the West Texas Intermediate, the U.S. benchmark, recently down 1% to $82.30 a barrel. Gold futures were down 3% at $3,575 an ounce, their lowest level in 14 months, while bitcoin continued losing ground, trading recently at $61,400.

Indexes on Track for Big Weekly Losses

Major stock indexes are on track to post their biggest weekly losses since the White House announced sweeping tariffs in April 2025. The Dow Jones Industrial was down about 6.2% for the week at Thursday's close, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were off by 5% and 5.1%, respectively. By comparison, the Dow dropped 7.9% during the first week of April last year, while the S&P tumbled 9.1% and the Nasdaq plunged 10%. Stocks have come under pressure in recent weeks as investors weigh the outlook for AI, which has fueled the market's growth in recent years.

Anthropic Shares Tumble After IPO Success

Anthropic (ANT) shares were down about 12% in recent premarket trading, after finishing their first trading session on Thursday about 17% above their IPO price. The stock opened on the Nasdaq at $111.50, quickly shot up to $115 and then mostly traded for less than $100. With shares priced at $83, the IPO raised a record $81.3 billion. Coming into today's session, the AI lab behind Claude has a market value of roughly $1.8 trillion, making it one of the world's most valuable companies by market capitalization. The IPO was viewed as an important test of the health of the AI trade.

Intuit Stock Drops Amid Mailchimp Sale

Intuit shares are plummeting after it announced plans to sell Mailchimp for about one-third of what it paid for the marketing automation platform. Intuit (INTU), the parent company, of TurboTax, Credit Karma and QuickBooks, plans to sell Mailchimp for about $3.68 billion. It paid about $12 billion for Mailchimp, according to an agreement Intuit announced in 2021. Intuit's shares were recently down nearly 10%, making it one of the worst performing stocks, even though the company reported quarterly results that beat expectations on the top and bottom lines.

Key Takeaways

Robinhood stock fell 29% in the past month as crypto trading slumped, and Coinbase fell even harder in the same selloff.

Robinhood's crypto revenue fell 55% in the third quarter and its October crypto volume fell 48%, but prediction markets now bring in more revenue than crypto, and deposits keep growing.

Kalshi handles an estimated 60% of Robinhood's prediction-market volume, and it reportedly plans to offer stock trading.

Analysts still expect a 38% jump in earnings in 2027, and the stock trades well below its three-year average multiple, so the drop looks like a chance to buy.

Robinhood Markets (HOOD:NASDAQ) stock is down 29% in the past month, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 10%. Crypto stocks had it worse: Coinbase (COIN:NASDAQ) is down 35%.

The two sold off like the same business. But crypto brought in only about 8% of Robinhood's third-quarter revenue, and prediction markets now bring in more.

Crypto did the damage, twice

Robinhood's third-quarter report on Oct. 27 showed revenue up 12% to a record $1.42 billion, a slowdown from 32% growth in the second quarter. Crypto revenue fell 55% to $120 million, while event-contract revenue rose more than 6x to $173 million. Operating expenses grew 16%, and GAAP diluted EPS fell 16% to $0.51, short of estimates. A $67 million unrealized loss on Robinhood Ventures Fund I took $0.07 off that, and adjusted EPS fell 3% to $0.60.

October was worse for crypto. Robinhood's crypto trading volume fell 48% from a year earlier to $17.0 billion. Binance's record $6.3 billion hack on Oct. 29 and a broad selloff on Nov. 5 also hit every crypto stock.

Coinbase has far more riding on that slump. Analysts expect its revenue to fall 28% this year and a normalized loss, yet it still trades at 76x forward earnings.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Robinhood, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Robinhood's Analyst Ratings

Kalshi went from partner to rival

On Nov. 16, The Wall Street Journal reported that Kalshi plans to launch stock and ETF trading within two months. That stings, since InGame estimated this summer that Kalshi handles about 60% of Robinhood's prediction-market volume. Robinhood keeps 1 cent of the 2-cent fee on each of those contracts.

Robinhood has some cushion. Rothera, its own exchange with Susquehanna, earned $28 million of that $173 million in third-quarter event-contract revenue. And on Nov. 12, the Justice Department and the CFTC sued Arkansas to stop it from enforcing its gambling laws against Kalshi, which lowers the risk that states shut the line down. Coinbase is hedging the same way: it works with Kalshi today and reportedly plans to bring its prediction markets in-house in 2027.

Why Did Nvidia Stock Fall 39%?

Today's big story: Will 2027 Be A 2022 Repeat For Stocks?

Nvidia has fallen 39% since Oct 6. Over the same time, a fund of chip stocks fell 29%, the Nasdaq 100 15% and the S&P 500 8%. Three events in early November took the blame. They were the midterm elections, the Nvidia board's investigation into reports about its CEO, Jensen Huang and a hot inflation report. We measured how much each one took, and what was left over.

The short answer: the selloff after the midterms and the Huang news, the board's investigation and his resignation, were real hits. They took about 9 and 11 points of Nvidia's fall. But Nvidia was already down 16% before either one. No single day in that slide was as bad as Nov 5. That slow slide is the bigger force.

How Much Did Each Event Take?

The biggest single day was political. On Nov 5, the day after Democrats won both houses of Congress, Nvidia fell 9.3%. The chip fund fell 11.2% and the S&P 500 fell 4.4%.

The board's investigation and Huang's Nov 12 resignation hit Nvidia alone. From Nov 9 to Nov 12, Nvidia fell 11.0%. The chip fund rose 8.1% over the same days. We covered that week in Will Nvidia Stock Go To $100?

The hot inflation report on Nov 10 did little by comparison. The S&P 500 fell only 0.4% that day.

Nvidia has dropped 39% in six weeks. A drop that deep is hard to sit through when your own savings are in it. The Trefis Income Solution fell less than the S&P 500 in each of the 9 big sell-offs since 2018, and it pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's. See how it held up.

What Is The Bigger Force?

The slide began right after long-term borrowing costs peaked. The 10-year Treasury yield is the interest rate on 10-year US government bonds. It hit 5.31% on Oct 5, its highest since 2002. The next day, the S&P 500 and Nvidia hit their highs. The 2-year yield tracks where the Fed is headed. It rose from 4.05% in June to 4.76% on Nov 19.

In our view, costly money hurts most where profits lie furthest in the future. And AI is the market's biggest bet on future profits.

At the same time, the big buyers' spare cash dried up. Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, Amazon and Oracle earned $607 billion over the last year. They kept just $33 billion as free cash, the cash left after capital spending. That is 5 cents of every dollar of profit. A year earlier, it was 53 cents.

Chicago, IL – November 20, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Nasdaq 100 Index ETF QQQ, Nvidia NVDA, Advanced Micro Devices AMD, SanDisk SNDK, Nebius Group NBIS, Arm Holdings ARM and Anthropic ANT

After the Huang Shock & Anthropic, Can Tech Find a Floor?
The Brutal (& Stealthy) Tech Bear Market

Having traded a plethora of difficult market environments, including COVID, the Global Financial Crisis, the Tariff Tantrum, and the 2022 bear market, I can confidently say that the 2026 market is one of the most difficult trading environments I can remember – if not the most difficult. The choppiness, whiplash, and violent direction changes make navigation challenging. Additionally, the sheer number of crosscurrents is more than I can ever remember. Until recently, higher oil prices and inflation concerns from the Iran War have weighed down stocks. Although oil prices have cooled significantly in recent weeks, the focus has turned to the AI trade. Despite unprecedented CAPEX spending, AI stocks have plunged.

Currently, the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index ETF is ~15% off its all-time highs, triggering a market correction. While QQQ has yet to trigger a technical bear market (defined as a 20% drawdown from highs), most AI stocks have been pummeled and are already in bear-market territory. Below are some examples of AI stocks and their % off highs:

Nvidia: -40%

Advanced Micro Devices: -26%

SanDisk: -68%

Nebius Group: -68%

Arm Holdings: -61%

The Tech Trade is Reaching a Tipping Point

As the old Wall Street saying goes, "Sometimes when you try to pick bottoms, all you end up with is stinky fingers." Currently, the bears are firmly in control of the market. The Nasdaq is below the 200-day moving average, AI's most important CEO is out of a job, and interest rates are expected to keep moving higher. 

For intermediate-term investors, it's critical to first and foremost protect capital and wait for confirmation in the form of improved market breadth and price rotation on higher time frames. If you need to reduce portfolio size, do so. The market is not going anywhere. Until then, avoid picking up pennies in front of a steamroller.

Nevertheless, if there's one thing that I have learned throughout my years of investing experience, it's that even if you're a spectator, the market is still worth following closely. That's because crisis ultimately equates to opportunity. Throughout American history, the market always exits these tough environments leading to massive opportunities. Additionally, equity markets are the master manipulator - bottoms are never obvious and often occur when they are least expected.
